items.title: Michael Rapino talks Live Nation's AI strategy, subscription ambitions for 14m-member All Access program, plus 3 other things to know from the firm's 2026 Investor Presentation
items.summary: At Live Nation's 2026 investor presentation, touring president Omar Al-Joulani said the year-old All Access fan membership programme already has 14 million members, who went to 34% more shows than they did over the previous three years. He said Live Nation is using its data and AI with All Access to sell more of its 20 million empty seats, and Michael Rapino called it a quiet little club with a big story over time as a membership subscription business. Rapino also said Live Nation will not hand its checkout or ticket inventory to AI platforms, and the company set a target of 33 million fans through its venues by 2031, up from 11 million.
items.what_it_means: The biggest promoter in live entertainment is treating a direct fan membership as a growth engine to fill unsold seats, and it is keeping that relationship and checkout to itself.

items.title: Vice City-themed night draws new fans to Heat game
items.summary: SBJ's roundup of local coverage says thousands of fans queued in heavy rain outside Kaseya Center for the Heat's GTA VI themed night against the Bucks. Figures provided by the Heat and reported by WPLG's Will Manso show more than 80% of ticket buyers were first-time buyers, and over 20% of those first-timers lived more than 250 miles away. Of fans who bought Vice City merchandise, 95% were first-time buyers at the team store, and over 30% of first-time orders were international.
items.what_it_means: Borrowing a bigger fandom from outside sport brought a largely new set of buyers to a regular-season game, which is the hard part of growing an audience.

items.title: Raiders give fans all access with new TikTok Live show
items.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders became the first NFL team to host an original pregame show on TikTok Live and have now run three episodes of Raiders All Access. The team's senior director of digital content strategy, Gavin Rivera, said the show was made for people outside Raiders fandom and even football fandom, using TikTok-native hosts and pop culture over analysis. The first episode, with an influencer interviewing Ice Cube, drew more than 220,000 unique viewers by the team's count, and the Raiders plan a show for every home game with potential sponsors later.
items.what_it_means: Teams are building shoulder programming specifically for people who are not yet fans, using platforms and hosts those people already follow.

items.title: Ally extends deals with popular women's sports platforms 'Welcome to the Party' and 'The RE-CAP Show'
items.summary: Ally has signed multiyear, multimillion-dollar extensions with the women's soccer platforms Welcome to the Party, hosted by Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy, and The RE-CAP Show, hosted by Tobin Heath and Christen Press. Ally has backed both since their origins and helped produce their first live shows, and RE-CAP grew listeners 47.1% and WTTP 154.5% from 2025 to 2026. Ally will be presenting sponsor of each flagship show, and in April it hit its 2022 pledge to split paid media equally between women's and men's sport, a year early.
items.what_it_means: A sponsor that backed women's sport media early is renewing on platforms it helped build, buying into the fan conversation around the game as well as the game itself.

items.title: LPGA Working With PGA Tour, Networks for Better TV Windows
items.summary: LPGA commissioner Craig Kessler said growth next year centres on collaborating with the PGA Tour and playing more events in network broadcast windows. The LPGA will have at least eight weekend slots on CBS or NBC directly after PGA Tour coverage in 2027, double this season, to benefit from the lead-in. Viewership this season was up 7% across all networks but flat on Golf Channel, and Kessler said fans who browse network channels discover the LPGA and tune in.
items.what_it_means: For a property still building its audience, a better slot on free-to-air network TV can be worth more than a bigger rights fee.

items.title: Dealmakers: Investors see sports' next growth wave beyond team ownership
items.summary: At SBJ's Dealmakers conference, investors from CVC, Muse Capital, Shamrock Capital and Goldman Sachs said the next growth wave lies in revenue streams built around teams, leagues and premium events. Steven Justman described an almost insatiable demand for premium live experiences, and Muse's Assia Grazioli called the female fan a very lucrative one to tap into. CVC's Marc Allera said the business of sport is immature relative to other media categories, with runway in media, sponsorship, hospitality, consumer products, real estate and direct fan relationships.
items.what_it_means: Institutional money increasingly values sport for the live experiences and fan relationships around the team, which raises the bar for how properties monetise them.

items.title: Scarcity, contracted revenue drive rising sports franchise values
items.summary: At SBJ's Dealmakers conference, Monumental's Zach Leonsis, Arctos co-founder Jordan Solomon and J.P. Morgan's Eric Menell said scarcity, contracted revenue and protective league structures keep franchise values rising, though prices like the Lakers' $12.5B sale are getting harder to finance. Leonsis said about 22 NBA teams had regional sports network partners last year against nine this year, and warned against confusing the decline of linear with where rights value remains. Asked about the biggest risk, Solomon pointed to the fan experience, saying teams are competing with sitting on the couch at home.
items.what_it_means: Even the investors driving record valuations name the in-venue fan experience as the biggest risk, because the couch is the competitor.

items.title: The WNBA's Audience Is Bigger Than Its Headlines
items.summary: Just Women's Sports founder Haley Rosen argues in an opinion piece that TV ratings show how many people watched the WNBA but not how much they care. She says her outlet's WNBA social posts drew 405 million views this season, with 70 players drawing at least 100,000 views and 42 topping one million. She argues coverage focused on a few stars and controversies leads brands to partner with the same few athletes, and says the real signal is where fans spend time between games.
items.what_it_means: Depth of fan engagement across many players points brands to a wider set of partnership options than TV ratings and star-led coverage suggest.

items.title: Bills, Sabres leverage venues to make Buffalo a major event destination
items.summary: SBJ's clip of Buffalo News reporting says the Bills and Sabres have made attracting major events to their venues part of their business plan. KeyBank Center is expected to host 193 events and draw 1.4 million people this year, and the new Highmark Stadium opens with six concerts in 2027 including Morgan Wallen, Zach Bryan, Metallica, Noah Kahan and Kenny Chesney. Business president Pete Guelli hopes the momentum leads to an NHL Stadium Series game in 2028 and the NFL Draft in 2029 or 2030.
items.what_it_means: Team owners are treating their venues as year-round event businesses, which makes concerts and tentpole events part of the sports franchise's commercial model.

items.title: Vivid Seats Hands Lenders 80% of Its Stock in $232M Debt Deal
items.summary: Vivid Seats agreed a recapitalisation with lenders that cuts its net debt by about $232 million of the $342 million it owes, adds $60 million in new financing and extends loan maturities to 2032. In return a lender group will own about 80% of the common stock, leaving existing shareholders with 20%. FOS reports the resale marketplace has been squeezed by pricing and inventory pressure from competitors and AI, debt, regulation and its own missteps, and its market value is around $29 million against nearly $2 billion at its 2021 listing.
items.what_it_means: The ticket resale middle layer is under real financial strain, as competition, regulation and AI pressure the economics of reselling access to live events.
